records.reason: The paper explicitly says it replicates the prediction linking toddler dysregulated fear to elevated social inhibition and names Buss et al. (2013); results state that the fear pattern predicted inhibition. Row 418 is Phelps et al. (2016), a separate EEG/coupling paper, not Buss et al. (2013).
records.omission_quote: The goals of the present study included (1) replication of identifying a pattern of dysregulated fear in toddlers (Buss, 2011) in a new sample; (2) replication of the prediction from toddler dysregulated fear to elevated social inhibition (Buss, 2011; Buss et al., 2013); and (3) extending our understanding of the implications of dysregulated fear for children’s development by linking this pattern of high fearfulness in low-threat contexts to physiological reactivity as a putative psychophysiological marker of dysregulated emotion processes in toddlerhood. Results were largely consistent with expectations—we were able to replicate the identification of children with dysregulated fear in this new sample, showed that this pattern of fear responding predicted inhibition across early childhood, and identified modest evidence for the idea that children who manifest a dysregulated fear pattern of behavior would also show a distinct pattern of physiological responding to laboratory challenges.
records.identity_quote: Buss KA, Davis EL, Kiel EJ, Brooker RJ, Beekman C, Early MC. Journal of Clinical Child & Adolescent Psychology. 2013. Dysregulated Fear Predicts Social Wariness and Social Anxiety Symptoms during Kindergarten; pp. 1–14.
